Terms.title: Terms of Service
Terms.s1Body: By creating an account or using Cigua, you agree to these Terms of Service. If you don't agree, please don't use the app.
Terms.s2Body: Cigua is a personal finance tracker that lets you record accounts, transactions, budgets, and subscriptions across currencies. It is a bookkeeping tool, not a bank, broker, or financial advisor, and it doesn't move money on your behalf.
Terms.s3Body: You're responsible for the accuracy of the information you enter and for keeping your login credentials secure. You must be able to form a binding contract to use Cigua, and one account is for one person — don't share credentials.
Terms.s4Body: Don't use Cigua to store data you don't have the right to store, attempt to disrupt the service, or try to access another user's data. We may suspend or terminate accounts that violate this.
Terms.s5Body: Balances, budgets, and insights shown in Cigua are calculated from the data you enter. They're provided for informational purposes only and are not financial, tax, or legal advice.
Terms.s6Body: How we collect, use, and store your data is described in the <privacyLink>Privacy Policy</privacyLink>. You can export or permanently delete your account and its data at any time from Settings.
Terms.s7Body: Cigua is provided “as is” without warranties of any kind. We don't guarantee the service will be uninterrupted or error-free, and to the fullest extent permitted by law we're not liable for any indirect or consequential damages arising from your use of it.
Terms.s8Body: We may update these terms from time to time. Continued use of Cigua after a change means you accept the updated terms.
Terms.s9Body: Questions about these terms? Reach us at <link>{email}</link>.

Privacy.title: Privacy Policy
Privacy.s1Body1: Account info: your email address, and, if you sign in with Google, your name and profile picture from your Google account.
Privacy.s1Body2: Financial data you enter: accounts, balances, transactions, budgets, and subscriptions. This data is entered by you and is not pulled from any bank or financial institution.
Privacy.s2Body: To run the app: authenticate you, show your data back to you, and calculate the balances, budgets, and insights the app displays. We don't sell your data or use it for advertising.
Privacy.s3Body: Cigua is built on Supabase, which hosts our database and handles authentication. If you sign in with Google, Google processes your sign-in under its own privacy policy. We don't share your financial data with any other third party.
Privacy.s4Body: Your data is stored in a database scoped to your account, protected by row-level security so only you can read or write it. Connections to Cigua are encrypted in transit.
Privacy.s5Body: We keep your data for as long as your account is active. You can permanently delete your account and all associated data at any time from Settings → Danger zone. Deletion is immediate and cannot be undone.
Privacy.s6Body: You can access, correct, or delete your data directly in the app at any time. If you'd like help exporting or removing your data, contact us using the details below.
Privacy.s7Body: We may update this policy from time to time. Continued use of Cigua after a change means you accept the updated policy.
Privacy.s8Body: Questions about this policy? Reach us at <link>{email}</link>.

Help.pageDescription: A field guide to every screen — from your first account to your monthly insights.
Help.gettingStartedIntro: Cigua sets you up in six short steps, and only the first two are required. Answer them once and the dashboard, budgets and "safe to spend" work from day one. Every step saves as you go, so if you refresh mid-setup you pick up where you left off.
Help.step1Body: Your name, the app's language, and the base currency your net worth and totals are measured in.
Help.step2Body: Your main checking, savings, cash or investment account and its current balance.
Help.step3Body: Add as many cards as you carry — name, currency and last 4 — and import each one's statement right there. Limit, closing day and due day fill themselves in.
Help.step4Body: Quincenal, monthly or weekly, your take-home pay and the account it lands in. This sets when your budgets reset and records your salary as recurring income. Irregular earners get calendar-month budgets.
Help.bankCalloutBody: Credit cards, loans, and bank selection all live on the full Accounts page instead — onboarding just needs one account to get you in the door. Add a bank once you have a second account, so transfers between them can qualify for the same-bank fee waiver.
Help.overviewIntro: Overview is home base — the first screen you land on after signing in. It's built to answer "where do I stand right now?" in one glance.
Help.overviewAvailable: Disponible — the big figure printed on the peso note: what you can still spend before your next payday, after everything already committed. The rows under it show how it adds up, and a timeline along the bottom edge marks the quincena from its start to payday, with today ticked.
Help.overviewNetWorth: Net worth — a smaller line on the same peso note: what you own minus what you owe, not what you can spend today.
Help.overviewStats: This period — a ruled table hanging off the note by a dashed line: income, paid out, and budget used so far, with a ruled meter for the budget.
Help.overviewUpcoming: Upcoming — a ledger of what's due next, one row each, with the date beside the amount: subscription charges and loan payments.
Help.overviewZeroState: No accounts yet? Overview shows a violet note with Import a statement first, then starter links to Accounts, Budgets, and Subscriptions, instead of an empty page.
Help.overviewFxWarning: If exchange rates can't be fetched, Overview and Insights say so — foreign holdings are counted 1:1 until rates return, and the warning tells you which currencies are affected.
Help.disponibleIntro: Disponible subtracts everything already committed before your next payday from your liquid balance:
Help.disponibleLiquid: Liquid balance — your checking, savings, and cash accounts. Investments and other assets don't count here: they're net worth, not money you can spend before your next paycheck.
Help.disponibleCommitted: Committed to goals — what you've already set aside for a savings goal.
Help.disponibleCards: Cards — each card's minimum payment on its outstanding balance, or the full balance if the card printed no minimum.
Help.disponibleLoans: Loans — installments due before the period ends.
Help.disponibleSubscriptions: Recurring — expenses due before the period ends. Recurring payments to a card or loan aren't counted twice; the card and loan rows already cover them.
Help.disponibleZeroCalloutTitle: Why is the full balance subtracted when the printed minimum is $0?
Help.disponibleZeroCalloutBody: A statement that prints a $0 minimum doesn't mean the card is settled — leave it unpaid, and you're still charged the full balance. That's why, when no minimum is printed, Disponible subtracts the card's full balance instead of zero: the line exists precisely to warn you about that case.
Help.disponiblePeriodNote: The period behind Disponible — monthly, semimonthly, or weekly — is set in Settings → Pay cycle, along with the day it anchors to.
Help.navNote: On mobile, Settings lives in the header, not the bottom nav. A floating Quick Add button for new transactions follows you everywhere.
Help.overviewMockCardsNote: Visa Infinite · full balance, no minimum printed
Help.accountsIntro: Everything you own or owe lives here, grouped into four sections: Accounts (checking, savings, cash, investment), Credit cards, Loans, and Property & assets.
Help.accountsAttention: "Needs a look" sits above everything else — overdue cards, cards due soon, and imports still waiting to be sorted, printed as a short ledger. Nothing to flag, and the whole section disappears, not even its heading.
Help.accountsCards: Every card is drawn as the physical object — art, network mark, last four digits — the same face wherever it appears. A card carrying more than one currency line (say a USD and a DOP balance on one physical card) shows that face once, with each line listed underneath as its own row rather than as a second card.
Help.accountsLoans: Loans and cuotas show the outstanding balance up top, then how many installments are paid drawn as a strip of perforated marks — solid ink for a paid cuota, a dashed outline for one still owed.
Help.quickAddCardNote: Need just a card, fast? Use "Quick add card" next to the Credit cards heading — it only asks for the name, currency, and last 4 digits, and you can fill in the limit and dates later from your first statement.
Help.cardGroupNote: A card group bundles multiple currency lines of one physical card (say, a USD and a CAD line) into a single entry.
Help.sameBankCalloutBody: Set the same bank on two accounts, and a Payment between them skips the network fee automatically — no toggling required.
Help.accountPageBalance: Balance (or amount owed) as the hero figure, plus a balance-over-time chart
Help.accountPageUtilization: Utilization and next due date, for credit cards
Help.accountPageSpend: A spend-by-category ledger for the current calendar month (a stamp, share and amount per category), for credit cards, counting only what was charged to that card and in that card's own currency
Help.accountPageAmortization: A full amortization schedule, for loans
Help.accountPageActivity: For checking, savings and investment accounts, the transfer tax and network fee settings plus what the account actually paid in fees and tax this year, across every kind of transaction; then the complete activity feed
Help.accountPageActions: Edit, Archive / Restore, or Delete (with a confirmation step)
Help.cardFaceBody: Credit cards are drawn as the physical object. Cigua reads the card's name to pick its colour and its network mark — an Amex Platinum comes out silver, a Visa Infinite black — and the face appears on the card's own page as well as in the list.
Help.cardFaceReroll: Not the colour you expected? Clear the colour field and save. Cigua guesses again from the name, and a colour you type in yourself is always kept as-is.
Help.accountPageFace: The card face, sitting beside the balance, so you know at a glance which card you're on.
Help.accountPageLines: For a card in a group, its other currency lines sit in a strip right under the face — one click to switch between them, and the group's name sits at the top of the page.
Help.subBrand: Logos and colours appear on their own — Cigua recognises the service from the name you gave it. Anything it doesn't recognise keeps its initial, which is a finished look, not a missing one. Renaming makes it look again.
Help.statementsBody: You can import a statement from several places: Overview asks for one when a statement is due, the Import statement button sits in the Wallet header and on the Insights cards that need one, each card's own page keeps it next to its history, and setup offers it at the end. If you have no card yet, you create one right there from three fields — name, currency and last 4 — because the limit, closing day and due day fill themselves in from the first statement. Upload the PDF — password-protected files are supported, with a retry if you mistype the password. Cigua splits it into sections (one per currency line on the card), you confirm which account each maps to — the dialog reads the statement back as a ruled sheet of the actual lines it will import — then Confirm to import. If a section is in a currency none of your card's lines uses, you can add that line right there instead of leaving to create it. Installments arrive as their own section carrying their own limit and balance, so they get their own line — named "· Installments" rather than "· DOP", so it doesn't read as a second card. This creates the underlying transactions and fills each card's report (cost of carry, cashback, fees) and the debt cost card in Insights. Cashback is every credit the bank itself gave you — rebates, promotions, bonuses — rather than your payments or a merchant's refund, and it's counted once per closing date, so re-importing the same PDF corrects the figure instead of doubling it. A few banks print a credit they never apply to their own closing balance — Banco Santa Cruz reverses the financing interest it charged you with a "Crédito por pago total" line when you pay in full, yet leaves that reversal out of the balance. Cigua keeps the line and badges it "Adjustment (no balance change)", but leaves it out of the totals and creates no transaction for it, so the statement's own arithmetic still ties and you are not credited money you never received. Statements up to 10 MB are accepted.
Help.triageBody: When an import finishes, the app categorises what it recognises and asks you about the rest — one merchant at a time, not one transaction at a time. Each merchant is a block on one ruled sheet: its lines and total on top, a row of category stamps beneath to pick from. Every answer is saved as a rule, so the next statement asks less, and when the last block is done a stamped mark closes the sheet. If you leave some of it, any statement takes you back to that screen from the card's page.
Help.triageMockMerchantOne: SM NACIONAL METRO PLZA SANTO DOMINGO-DO
Help.transactionsIntro: Three kinds of entry cover everything: Expense, Income, and Payment. Each prints as one ruled line in the ledger, led by the category's ink stamp, grouped under its date. Expenses show a minus sign, income a plus in teal, and payments carry no sign.
Help.typePayment: Payment — a transfer between your own accounts, or paying down a credit card or loan. Cross-currency payments show a live "lands as X" preview of the converted amount.
Help.toggleTax: Transfer tax — charged when money leaves your checking or savings account. Moving money between your own cash and bank accounts is free of it; so is spending cash or swiping a card, since no account is debited. Paying a credit card or a loan is taxed, because that money goes to the bank even though the card is in your name.
Help.toggleFee: Network fee — off unless you add it, because only some transfers carry one. Always waived within the same bank.
Help.addingBody: Quick Add prints as a paper slip that opens on the amount with a numeric keypad: type it, tap a category stamp, save. The stamps are ordered by the categories you use most, and the account is the source of your last expense or payment. More details opens every remaining field — destination, rate, date, notes, budget exclusion and the tax and fee switches — in the same slip. To start from the full form instead, use Add transaction on an account's page. Every entry takes a free-text Note, the one field that stays editable on statement-imported rows, where the description belongs to your bank.
Help.findingBody: Search matches a transaction's description, its notes, and — when you type a figure like 1,500 — its amount. Filters run against your whole history, not just what's on screen, and the ledger loads more as you scroll until it tells you you've reached the end. Each day's date stays pinned at the top of the screen while you scroll through its lines.
Help.merchantCalloutBody: Transactions created from a statement import keep their original amount and date locked — you just confirm the category, and can save "always categorize this merchant" so it's automatic next time.
Help.budgetsIntro: Budgets run month by month, one row per category. Navigate between months, and set an amount for each category inline.
Help.budgetsCategory: Create categories with a name, emoji, and color
Help.budgetsInline: Type a monthly amount directly into a category's row
Help.budgetsProgress: Near and over are marked, not just colored: a Near tag and a heavier rule as you approach the limit, an Over budget flag and a double-rule end once you pass it
Help.budgetsHeader: The peso note at the top carries the period's budget total, with the amount used and what's left underneath
Help.copyCalloutBody: Duplicates last month's amounts forward, so you're not re-typing the same numbers every month.
Help.subscriptionsIntro: Save the expenses and payments you repeat — streaming, rent, a transfer to savings, a card payment — and record each occurrence in one tap.
Help.subName: Pick Expense or Payment, then set a name, amount and currency
Help.subCycle: Choose a cycle — weekly, semimonthly (quincenal), monthly, yearly, or custom. Each anchors to a day
Help.subLink: An expense takes the account it's paid from and a category; a payment takes a from and a to account
Help.subFees: From checking or savings you can apply the transfer tax and network fee. A card charge never carries them
Help.subViews: Recurring is one ledger ordered by next charge date, with income above a double rule and paused items last. Toggle each one active or paused
Help.subLogCharge: The page totals your monthly-equivalent amount and shows each one's next date. When it actually happens, hit Record: the transaction is saved with everything you set up, dated today. If a month differs, edit that transaction in the ledger.
Help.insightsIntro: Insights answers four questions: is your net worth moving, where did the money go, are you on pace, and what does your debt cost. The middle band follows the month you pick; the others don't need one.
Help.insightsSpend: Spend ledger: where your money went, one stamped row per category with its share
Help.insightsDebt: Debt health: credit utilization and loan payoff at a glance
Help.insightsCashflow: Cash-flow trend and spending pace across the month
Help.insightsBudget: Expenses vs. budget, category by category
Help.insightsBasis: Two of these count money differently, on purpose. Spend distribution and spending pace count a purchase the day you make it, card charges included — that is where your money went. Expenses vs. budget, and the spending figure on Overview, count it the day it leaves an account, so a card charge lands when you pay the statement. Card payments and transfers between your own accounts never count as spending on either: the purchases behind them are already counted.
Help.askIntro: A text box that answers questions about your own numbers in plain words — English or Spanish, whichever you're using. Cigua reads your data to answer, and writes back the real figures — a sentence for one number, a table when you've asked about a stretch of transactions.
Help.askAnswers: Good questions: spending by category over any date range, what went on one specific card between two dates, what a balance is now, what's due and when, how a month tracked against its budget.
Help.askReadOnly: It can only read. There is no question you can ask that changes a transaction, a budget, or an account — and it only ever sees your own data, never anyone else's.
Help.askLimits: It answers from what's recorded. If you haven't imported a statement or logged a transaction, it can't know about it — and it will say so rather than guess.
Help.askMockQuestion: How much did I spend on transportation last month?
Help.askMockAnswer: RD$8,420 across 14 transactions — about 12% more than June.
Help.settingsPayCycle: Pay cycle — monthly, semimonthly, or weekly, with the anchor day that decides when Disponible and your budgets reset.
Help.settingsTheme: Theme — light or dark, from here or the sidebar
Help.settingsAccount: Sign out, or delete your account (with confirmation)
Help.rulesBody: Settings → Category rules holds everything the app has learned: the text it looks for in a transaction, and the category it assigns. The number says how many lines of your statements match that rule — one matching 40 lines is working, one matching 0 probably has a typo. You can shorten the text so it covers every branch of a merchant. Editing a rule changes future imports; it does not recategorise what you already saved.
Help.budgetGroupsIntro: A category says what an expense was. A group says what it counts against. Keeping the two apart lets you name your spending precisely without your monthly plan turning into a list of forty lines.
Help.budgetGroupsQualifier: Category: Groceries, Fuel, Rent. Specific, and you can have as many as you like.
Help.budgetGroupsGroup: Group: Essentials, Lifestyle, Future. Coarse, and most people want between three and six.
Help.budgetGroupsAssign: Each category is assigned to a group from its own dialog, and every expense in that category inherits it.
Help.budgetGroupsOverride: A single expense can count under a different group without leaving its category: that Uber stays Transport in your reports and counts under Lifestyle in your plan.
Help.budgetGroupsOptionalBody: If you never create a group, the Budgets page looks and works exactly as it always has. Your category budgets are still there and still count.
Help.footerNote: This guide mirrors the app's own navigation, top to bottom.
Help.insightsDebtCost: What your debt costs, in two groups never added together: what each card would charge if you financed its balance (from its latest statement), and the interest each loan payment actually went to. Tap a row to open that card or loan.
Help.accountPageReport: For credit cards, a card report: cost of carry from the latest statement, interest paid, cashback and fees & insurance this year, penalty fees, what you paid into the card this month, and welcome-bonus progress. Rows appear only once there's data behind them.
Help.step5Body: Describe each loan as it stands today: what you owe, the installment, the annual rate and the payment day. The installments left are worked out from the rate; if you don't know it, enter the count under More details. Each becomes a loan account whose installments show up in upcoming payments.
Help.step6Body: Tap the bills you pay every month — rent, electricity, water, internet, phone, insurance — and give each an amount and day. They're subtracted from "safe to spend" before they're due.
